idiom_name: one handler per route + transport-free domain entry point + separate response builder
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: let the router or Front Controller choose one Action for the method/path. The Action copies only transport inputs into plain values or a DTO, invokes a Domain entry point that receives no request, session or framework object, and invokes a Responder that owns status, headers, cookies, negotiation, formatting and body. Keep business branches and validation in the Domain and representation branches in the Responder; the router may preflight Acceptability but must not become the business layer. Storage-backed sessions, authentication and authorization normally belong behind the Domain, while an anonymity check may stay at routing. Where one action serves several representations, select or compose the format-specific Responder before expensive Domain work when the framework permits it.
code_sketch:
# routing table: (method, path) -> action
def handle_show_user(request):           # Action
    user_id = request.path('id')        # collect input, no business logic
    result  = domain.find_user(user_id) # Domain: plain values in, payload out
    return responder.show_user(result)  # Responder builds status/headers/body
# the domain entry point is callable from a CLI or a queue consumer unchanged
pitfalls: Putting validation, authorization or a business branch in the Action -> the handler becomes a fat controller, and callers cannot reuse the rule without HTTP plumbing -> pass plain input to the Domain and return a Domain Payload.

Passing the HTTP request, session or framework response into the Domain -> transport types leak into business tests and CLI/message callers -> translate at the Action and keep Domain signatures transport-neutral.

Letting the Responder query storage for widgets, translations or counters -> presentation owns hidden Domain dependencies and can disagree with the Domain result -> include all needed data in the Domain Payload.
Returning a Responder for the router to invoke later -> a second caller must know presentation lifecycle and can mutate the boundary -> invoke it inside the Action and return the built response.

Putting every HTTP method for a resource behind one Action with a request.method switch -> the handler becomes a Page Controller with a hidden dispatch table -> register one Action per route and let the router dispatch.

Replacing endpoint classes with one generic callable triple for the entire application -> dependency wiring and route-specific input rules disappear into indirection -> reserve the generic Action for framework infrastructure and keep application Actions explicit.

Wrapping a trivial one-format read in three classes -> navigation and wiring cost more than the separation -> keep one thin handler until a second representation, consumer or meaningful test seam justifies ADR.

Injecting every endpoint's collaborators into one shared controller constructor (action injection) -> the controller needs container acrobatics per method and actions leak state through shared fields -> split each endpoint into its own Action class receiving exactly its dependencies.

Deciding status-bearing responses like 304 Not Modified or 404 Not Found inside the Responder by re-reading storage or recomputing state -> presentation duplicates domain decisions and can disagree with the domain result -> let the Domain report not-found or not-modified in the payload and have the Responder only map it to status and headers.

Treating the Domain role as a licence for procedure-only scripts that shuffle DTOs -> business invariants scatter across actions and the model goes anemic while looking layered -> keep the rules in a Domain Model or richer service behind the Domain entry point.
sources: Jones, Paul M., Action Domain Responder (2014) - components, collaborations and the ADR-vs-Model-2 comparison. https://paul-m-jones.com/adr/
Fowler, Martin, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (2002) - Page Controller, the controller style ADR replaces for single-request endpoints.
